items.t: Announced, as Vice Chair of the Legislative Women's Caucus, the introduction of SB 233 to allow Arizona reproductive care providers to perform abortion services in California under an expedited licensing process.
items.q: announced the introduction of new abortion rights legislation today, responding to Arizona’s sweeping ban on reproductive care. An urgency measure, SB 233 would allow Arizona reproductive care providers to immediately perform abortion services in California

items.t: Said access to healthcare should not require a state of emergency or depend on a person's location, mobility, or income.
items.q: Access to healthcare should not require a state of emergency, nor depend upon a person’s location, mobility, or income.

items.t: Proposed Assembly Bill 2292 to raise state rates for infant and toddler care, create a grant program for new child care facilities, and establish a fund to recruit family child care providers.
items.q: Assembly Bill 2292 will strategically invest in California's child care system by increasing state rates for infant and toddler care, creating a grant program to fund implementation and start- up costs of new child care facilities

record.t: Was elected Chair of the California Legislative Women's Caucus for the 2025-2026 session by a vote of acclamation.
record.q: In a vote of acclamation, the LWC membership elected Assembly Majority Leader Cecilia Aguiar-Curry (D-Winters) as its Chair and Senator Monique Limón (D-Santa Barbara) as its Vice Chair.

record.t: Became the first woman elected as Mayor of Winters.
record.q: Assemblywoman Aguiar-Curry, 62 made history in the small town of Winters when she became the first woman elected as Mayor.

record.t: Announced that Governor Newsom signed Assembly Bill 1987, which provides a more reliable source of funding to maintain California's State Wildlife Areas.
record.q: announced today that Governor Newsom has signed Assembly Bill 1987 ( AB 1987 ), legislation that will provide a more reliable source of funding to maintain California’s State Wildlife Areas.

record.t: Authored Assembly Bill 1890, which was signed into law by Governor Newsom to strengthen housing for farmworkers.
record.q: Assembly Bill 1890 ( AB 1890 ), authored by Assembly Majority Leader Cecilia Aguiar-Curry (D-Winters), was signed into law by Governor Newsom, strengthening housing for the farmworkers

record.t: Announced that Governor Newsom signed Assembly Bill 1857 into law, intended to help communities bring grocery stores back.
record.q: announced Governor Newsom signed Assembly Bill 1857 ( AB 1857 ) into law, helping communities bring grocery stores back, increase competition and expand access to healthy, affordable food.

record.t: Announced that Governor Newsom signed Assembly Bill 706, the FOREST and Wildfire Prevention Fund Act.
record.q: announced today that Governor Newsom signed Assembly Bill 706 ( AB 706 ), the Forest Organic Residue, Energy, and Safety Transformation (FOREST) and Wildfire Prevention Fund Act.

record.t: Announced that Governor Newsom signed Assembly Bill 2250 into law to close enforcement gaps in California's cannabis and hemp laws.
record.q: today announced Governor Newsom signed Assembly Bill 2250 ( AB 2250 ) into law, to close enforcement gaps in California’s cannabis and hemp laws

record.t: Announced that Governor Newsom signed Assembly Bill 52, which codifies two advisory committees created by the California Department of Food and Agriculture.
record.q: announced today that Governor Newsom has signed Assembly Bill 52 ( AB 52 ), legislation that codifies two advisory committees created by the California Department of Food and Agriculture (CDFA)

record.t: Authored Assembly Bill 1973, which was signed by Governor Newsom to remove barriers for advanced practice clinicians providing reproductive healthcare.
record.q: Assembly Bill 1973 ( AB 1973 ), authored by Assembly Majority Leader Cecilia Aguiar-Curry (D-Winters), was signed by Governor Newsom to remove outdated barriers that prevent qualified advanced practice clinicians

record.t: Announced that the Legislature passed Assembly Bill 1906 to expand cervical cancer screening access.
record.q: announced today that the California State Legislature passed Assembly Bill 1906 ( AB 1906 ), legislation to expand cervical cancer screening access

record.t: Introduced Assembly Bill 32 to make telehealth flexibilities permanent under state law.
record.q: Assembly Bill (AB) 32. Introduced in December to highlight the pressing need to strengthen telehealth access during this legislative session, AB 32 seeks to make current telehealth flexibilities permanent under state law.
